title: Acts Chapter 16 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 16 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 16 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 16.

questions.question: In Acts 16, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Lydia was a seller of purple
questions.explanation: This is correct because Acts 16:1 states that Paul came to Derbe and Lystra first.

questions.question: What was the name of the disciple mentioned in Acts 16?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:1 specifically mentions a certain disciple named Timotheus.

questions.question: Who was Timotheus's mother?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:1 states that Timotheus was the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess.

questions.question: What was Timotheus's father's nationality?
questions.explanation: According to Acts 16:1, Timotheus's father was a Greek.

questions.question: What action did Paul take regarding Timotheus?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:3 states that Paul took and circumcised Timotheus because of the Jews.

questions.question: What did Paul and his companions deliver as they went through the cities?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:4 mentions that they delivered the decrees for to keep that were ordained of the apostles.

questions.question: What was the result of their efforts in the churches?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:5 states that the churches were established in the faith and increased in number daily.

questions.question: In which region were Paul and his companions forbidden to preach?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:6 indicates that they were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia.

questions.question: What did Paul see in a vision?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:9 describes a vision in which a man of Macedonia stood and prayed to Paul.

questions.question: What city did Paul and his companions come to after Troas?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:11 states that they came with a straight course to Samothracia and the next day to Neapolis.

questions.question: What was Lydia's occupation?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:14 mentions that Lydia was a seller of purple.

questions.question: True or False: Timotheus was well reported of by the brethren.
questions.explanation: Acts 16:2 states that Timotheus was well reported of by the brethren at Lystra and Iconium.

questions.question: True or False: The Holy Ghost allowed them to preach in Asia.
questions.explanation: Acts 16:6 indicates that the Holy Ghost forbade them to preach in Asia, making the statement false.

questions.question: True or False: Lydia was from the city of Troas.
questions.explanation: Acts 16:14 states that Lydia was from the city of Thyatira, not Troas.

questions.question: True or False: Paul received a letter from the apostles in Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Acts 16:4 mentions decrees ordained of the apostles, but does not indicate that Paul received a letter.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 16 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 16 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Lydia do after she was baptized?
options: She constrained Paul and Silas to come into her house.
She returned to her old ways.
questions.correctAnswer: She constrained Paul and Silas to come into her house.
questions.explanation: This is correct as stated in Acts 16:15, where Lydia besought them and constrained them to come into her house.

questions.question: What does Acts 16:17 promise will happen if someone acknowledges the servants of God?
options: They will show the way of salvation.
questions.correctAnswer: They will show the way of salvation.
questions.explanation: This reflects the proclamation made by the damsel in Acts 16:17, where she identifies Paul and his companions as servants of the most high God who show the way of salvation.

questions.question: What caused Paul to command the spirit to come out of the damsel?
options: He wanted to show his authority.
He was grieved by her actions.
questions.correctAnswer: He was grieved by her actions.
questions.explanation: As stated in Acts 16:18, Paul was grieved and turned to command the spirit to come out of her.

questions.question: How did the masters of the damsel react after Paul cast out the spirit?
options: They caught Paul and Silas and brought them to the rulers.
questions.correctAnswer: They caught Paul and Silas and brought them to the rulers.
questions.explanation: This is verified in Acts 16:19, where the masters saw their hope of gain was gone and took action against Paul and Silas.

questions.question: According to Acts 16:22, what happened to Paul and Silas after being accused?
options: They were beaten and cast into prison.
questions.correctAnswer: They were beaten and cast into prison.
questions.explanation: Acts 16:22 states that the multitude rose against them, and the magistrates commanded them to be beaten.

questions.question: What were Paul and Silas doing at midnight in prison?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:25 mentions that at midnight, Paul and Silas prayed and sang praises to God.

questions.question: What event occurred suddenly while Paul and Silas were in prison?
options: A great earthquake shook the foundations of the prison.
questions.correctAnswer: A great earthquake shook the foundations of the prison.
questions.explanation: This is described in Acts 16:26, where a great earthquake occurred, leading to the prison doors being opened.

questions.question: What did the jailer intend to do when he awoke and saw the prison doors open?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:27 states that the jailer drew out his sword and was about to kill himself, thinking the prisoners had escaped.

questions.question: What did Paul tell the jailer when he saw him about to harm himself?
options: Do not harm yourself, for we are all here.
questions.correctAnswer: Do not harm yourself, for we are all here.
questions.explanation: In Acts 16:28, Paul cried out to the jailer not to harm himself because all the prisoners were still present.

questions.question: Acts 16:24 indicates that Paul and Silas were placed in what part of the prison?
questions.explanation: According to Acts 16:24, they were thrust into the inner prison and their feet were fastened in stocks.

questions.question: What is a key lesson from Acts 16:25 regarding faith in difficult situations?
options: To pray and sing praises to God.
questions.correctAnswer: To pray and sing praises to God.
questions.explanation: Acts 16:25 illustrates the importance of maintaining faith through prayer and praise even in prison.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the role of the Holy Spirit in Acts 16:6-7?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:6-7 shows how Paul and his companions were guided by the Holy Spirit in their mission, preventing them from preaching in certain regions.

questions.question: True or False: Lydia was a seller of purple from Thyatira.
questions.explanation: This is true as stated in Acts 16:14, where Lydia is identified as a seller of purple from Thyatira.

questions.question: True or False: The magistrates praised Paul and Silas for their teachings.
questions.explanation: This is false; instead, the magistrates ordered them to be beaten as mentioned in Acts 16:22.

questions.question: True or False: The earthquake caused only Paul to be set free from prison.
questions.explanation: This is false, as Acts 16:26 states that all the doors were opened and everyone's bands were loosed, not just Paul.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 16 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 16.

questions.question: What did the keeper of the prison do when he realized the prison doors were open?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:27 describes that the keeper of the prison, upon awakening and seeing the open doors, drew out his sword, intending to kill himself, believing the prisoners had escaped.

questions.question: What did Paul and Silas tell the jailer he must do to be saved?
options: Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: In Acts 16:31, Paul and Silas instructed the jailer to believe on the Lord Jesus Christ for salvation.

questions.question: What did the jailer do immediately after believing?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:33 states that the jailer took Paul and Silas and washed their stripes after he believed, showing his transformation and repentance.

questions.question: What was the response of the magistrates when they learned Paul and Silas were Romans?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:38 indicates that the serjeants reported to the magistrates that Paul and Silas were Romans, which caused them to fear because they had beaten and imprisoned them unlawfully.

questions.question: What did the jailer do after bringing Paul and Silas into his house?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:34 describes that after bringing Paul and Silas into his house, the jailer set meat before them, rejoicing with all his house after believing in God.

questions.question: What was the specific message Paul and Silas shared with the jailer?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:32 states that Paul and Silas spoke the word of the Lord to the jailer and all in his house, which included the message of salvation.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'sōtēria' in Acts 16:30 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Sōtēria' (σωτηρία) means 'deliverance' or 'salvation' in Greek, which is the context of the jailer's plea in Acts 16:30.

questions.question: What literary device is exemplified in Acts 16:31 with the phrase 'and thou shalt be saved, and thy house'?
questions.explanation: The phrase in Acts 16:31 shows parallelism as it emphasizes both the jailer's salvation and that of his household, highlighting the inclusiveness of the promise.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of salvation found in Acts 16:31?
questions.explanation: John 3:16, Romans 10:9, and Ephesians 2:8 all emphasize the theme of salvation through belief in Jesus Christ, echoing the message in Acts 16:31.

questions.question: Which verse comes immediately before Acts 16:29?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:28 precedes 16:29, where Paul cries out to the jailer to do himself no harm, as they are all present in the prison.

questions.question: What did the magistrates command to be done to Paul and Silas in Acts 16:22?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:22 states that the magistrates commanded to beat Paul and Silas after the multitude rose up against them.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'baptizō' in Acts 16:33 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Baptizō' (βαπτίζω) means 'to immerse' in Greek, which is the action taken by the jailer and his household as a sign of their faith in Acts 16:33.

questions.question: The jailer's belief led him to do what immediately after being baptized?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:34 indicates that after the jailer was baptized, he set meat before Paul and Silas, showing hospitality and rejoicing in his faith.

questions.question: True or False: Paul and Silas were released from prison without any further issues.
questions.explanation: Paul and Silas were not released immediately; they insisted on a public acknowledgment of their Roman citizenship, as stated in Acts 16:37.

questions.question: True or False: Lydia was the first person converted in Philippi.
questions.explanation: Acts 16:14 shows that Lydia was the first recorded convert in Philippi, as she attended to the things spoken by Paul, indicating her conversion.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 16 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 16 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 16:3 teach about the relationship between cultural identity and covenantal inclusion in the church?
options: Circumcision is necessary to affirm Jewish identity for ministry
Gentiles must fully adopt Jewish customs to be saved
Salvation transcends ethnic boundaries but respects cultural sensitivities
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation transcends ethnic boundaries but respects cultural sensitivities
questions.explanation: Acts 16:3 shows Paul circumcising Timothy because of the Jews in those quarters, indicating respect for cultural customs without making them salvation requirements.

questions.question: What doctrine about the guidance of the Holy Spirit is taught in Acts 16:6-7?
options: The Holy Spirit sovereignly directs missionary activity
The Holy Spirit only guides apostles
Human plans override the Spirit's guidance
The Spirit forbids all preaching in Gentile regions
questions.correctAnswer: The Holy Spirit sovereignly directs missionary activity
questions.explanation: Acts 16:6-7 describes Paul and his companions being forbidden by the Holy Spirit to preach in Asia and Bithynia, showing the Spirit's sovereign control over mission.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding divine calling and evangelism is taught in Acts 16:9-10?
options: God calls believers to specific mission fields
Evangelism must be self-directed without visions
All visions are symbolic and non-binding
Missionary work is optional for believers
questions.correctAnswer: God calls believers to specific mission fields
questions.explanation: Acts 16:9-10 reveals Paul's vision of the Macedonian man calling them over, demonstrating God's specific calling for evangelistic outreach.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 16:25 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:25 shows Paul and Silas praying and singing praises in prison at midnight, demonstrating God's providential care sustaining them in suffering.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly demonstrated in Acts 16:31 when Paul and Silas reply to the jailer?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:31 emphasizes salvation by faith in Jesus Christ for the jailer and his household, showcasing God's mercy to sinners.

questions.question: How does Acts 16:9-10 connect to the broader redemptive theme of the inclusion of Gentiles in the Church?
options: It initiates the missionary journey into Europe fulfilling God's promise to Abraham
It limits the gospel to Jewish territories only
It shows the failure of Gentile evangelism
It emphasizes the rejection of Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: It initiates the missionary journey into Europe fulfilling God's promise to Abraham
questions.explanation: The vision directing Paul to Macedonia marks the gospel's advance into Europe, fulfilling God's promise to bless all nations through Abraham's seed.

questions.question: In what way does the deliverance of Paul and Silas in Acts 16:26-28 prefigure Christ's resurrection?
options: It symbolizes liberation from death and bondage
It shows the final judgment of sinners
It represents the end of all suffering
It illustrates the failure of faith
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes liberation from death and bondage
questions.explanation: The earthquake freeing them from prison bonds in Acts 16:26-28 is a typological foreshadowing of Christ's resurrection breaking the power of sin and death.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 16:14 and 16:15 teach about the role of divine grace and human response in salvation?
options: God opens hearts enabling faith, which leads to baptism and hospitality
Salvation is purely human effort without divine intervention
Baptism precedes faith as a work to earn salvation
Divine grace is limited to men only
questions.correctAnswer: God opens hearts enabling faith, which leads to baptism and hospitality
questions.explanation: Acts 16:14 shows the Lord opening Lydia's heart to attend to Paul's message, and 16:15 describes her baptism and welcoming Paul, illustrating grace enabled faith and obedient response.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about spiritual warfare and authority is taught by Acts 16:17 and 16:18?
options: Believers have authority over demonic spirits through Jesus' name
Demons have ultimate power over believers
Spiritual gifts are independent of Christ's authority
Demonic possession is irrelevant to Christian mission
questions.correctAnswer: Believers have authority over demonic spirits through Jesus' name
questions.explanation: Acts 16:17-18 shows Paul commanding the spirit to come out in Jesus' name, teaching that believers exercise authority over demons by Christ's power.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about suffering and witness does Acts 16:22-25 teach?
options: Suffering for the gospel is part of sanctification and leads to witness
Christians should avoid suffering at all costs
questions.correctAnswer: Suffering for the gospel is part of sanctification and leads to witness
questions.explanation: Acts 16:22-25 depict Paul and Silas beaten and imprisoned, yet praying and singing, showing sanctification through suffering and ongoing witness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the imprisonment of Paul and Silas in Acts 16:22-24 shows that Christianity promotes civil disobedience. What does Acts 16:22-40 actually teach?
options: Paul asserts his Roman rights and seeks legal redress, affirming respect for civil authority
Paul encourages violent rebellion against magistrates
The apostles reject all forms of government
questions.correctAnswer: Paul asserts his Roman rights and seeks legal redress, affirming respect for civil authority
questions.explanation: Verses 16:37-39 show Paul demanding the magistrates fetch them out publicly because they were beaten unlawfully, demonstrating respect for lawful process, not rebellion.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 16:1-2 teach about the importance of Christian reputation within the community for effective ministry?
options: Good testimony among believers is essential for ministry effectiveness
Only miraculous signs grant ministry credibility
questions.correctAnswer: Good testimony among believers is essential for ministry effectiveness
questions.explanation: Acts 16:2 notes Timothy was well reported of by brethren, showing the importance of a good reputation for ministry partnership.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially demonstrated in Acts 16:9 where Paul receives the Macedonian vision?
questions.explanation: God's sovereign direction of Paul's mission through a vision in Acts 16:9 reveals divine control over salvation history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about faith and household salvation is taught in Acts 16:31 and 16:33?
options: Faith in Christ leads to salvation of both the believer and their household
Only individuals are saved, not households
questions.correctAnswer: Faith in Christ leads to salvation of both the believer and their household
questions.explanation: Acts 16:31 promises salvation to the jailer and his house; 16:33 records him and his household baptized, showing household inclusion through faith.

questions.question: How does the episode in Acts 16:16-18 deepen the biblical understanding of spiritual authority in the name of Jesus?
options: It reveals that believers exercise authority over unclean spirits by Jesus' name
It teaches that spiritual powers are autonomous
It denies any authority over spirits
It shows that only apostles can exercise spiritual authority
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals that believers exercise authority over unclean spirits by Jesus' name
questions.explanation: Paul commanding the spirit to come out in Acts 16:18 shows the authority believers have in Jesus' name over evil spirits.
